title: Veil and Ember Again
premise: Wendell Fairweather has spent twelve years swallowing poison for the crown, building immunity dish by dish while memorizing every smuggler's path through the Thornfell mountains. When the old gods stir and answer prayers again, Wendell discovers the king he serves is already dead — replaced by a hollow vessel wearing his face, animated by a god-hungry usurper who needs the taster's poisoned blood to finish the binding. Fleeing into the mountains with a disgraced priestess and the king's true heir, Wendell must choose between loyalty to a crown that never protected him and truth that could shatter the realm. In the end, Wendell uses his immunity as a weapon, feeding the usurper a final dose of every poison in his blood to unbind the false king — saving the free cities at the cost of the last shred of his own survival.
about_author: K. M. Kavanagh is a former line cook turned fantasy novelist who swears the best plot ideas arrive during dinner rush. They live near real mountains that are considerably less haunted than Thornfell.

chapters.title: The Taster's Oath
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. A routine tasting at court goes wrong when a dish he survives should have killed him — and the court physician quietly notes it. Wendell realizes someone is testing him, not the king. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine; the first crack in his carefully managed life.

chapters.title: Prayers with Teeth
chapters.summary: Priestess Sera Vane's POV. In a shuttered shrine, Sera prays to a god dead for two centuries — and it answers. She witnesses the old magic returning across Thornfell and is branded a heretic for reporting it. Emotional beat: terror and wonder entwined; faith rekindled at the worst possible moment.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Summoned to a private audience, Wendell tastes the king's wine and realizes the man before him has no scent, no pulse-beat behind the eyes — a vessel. The physician who tested him is found dead. Emotional beat: cold horror; loyalty curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: Wendell flees east through Thornfell using smuggler paths only he knows, pursued by the usurper's riders. He collides with Sera and a half-starved boy, Tam, whom she insists is the king's hidden heir. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance forged in flight; trust extended under duress.

chapters.title: Salt and Sovereignty
chapters.summary: Sera's POV. Hiding in a free-city safehouse, Sera teaches Wendell what the returning gods want: a mortal whose body holds death itself — his immune blood — to break or complete bindings. Tam's claim to the throne is verified by an old rite. Emotional beat: burden of purpose; Wendell resents being chosen.

chapters.title: The Ember Vigil
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. At a mountain shrine, Wendell undergoes the vigil: the old god shows him the night the real king died and the usurper's bargain. He sees his own death waiting at the end of one path. Emotional beat: grief and resolve; accepting a price he cannot yet name.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Ford
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. A trusted ally sells their route to the usurper's general; Tam is captured crossing the river. Sera is wounded holding the ford while Wendell escapes upstream. Emotional beat: devastation; loyalty shattered by the price of survival others were willing to pay.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Tam's POV (brief) then Wendell's. Tam endures the usurper's court, learning the vessel-king weeps when no one watches. Wendell returns alone through enemy lines, trading on his old reputation as loyal taster to get inside. Emotional beat: quiet courage; walking back into the trap willingly.

chapters.title: Every Poison I Have Ever Survived
chapters.summary: Climax. Wendell's POV. Before the assembled court, Wendell offers himself as the binding's final ingredient — then turns the ritual inside out, letting the usurper drink his accumulated poisons. The vessel-king collapses free of the binding; the usurper burns from within. Emotional beat: sacrificial triumph; justice outside any law.

chapters.title: A Dish Worth Eating
chapters.summary: Sera's POV, closing with Wendell's. Wendell survives, barely — the gods' return bought him a slow recovery instead of a grave. Tam is crowned regent under Sera's guidance; Wendell declines a title and opens a tavern at the mountain's foot. Emotional beat: hard-won peace; survival finally feeling like living.
